description: NF discovery operation for locating NF instances and associated NF service instances via the NRF, including same-PLMN, different-PLMN, redirecting/forwarding NRF, and target-PLMN resolution scenarios.
normative_statements: The NF Service Consumer shall send an HTTP GET request to the resource URI "nf-instances" collection resource.
The input filter criteria for the discovery request shall be included in query parameters.

Upon receiving a discovery request for complete NF profiles, the NRF shall verify that the requesting entity is authorized to discover the complete profile of NF instances, based on local policies or the receipt of an access token granting such permission.
If the requesting entity is not authorized to discover complete NF profiles, the NRF shall reject the request or handle it as a service discovery request without access to the complete profile.

When certain query parameters in the discovery request are not supported by the NRF, the NRF shall ignore the unsupported query parameters and continue processing the request with the rest of the query parameters.
On success, "200 OK" shall be returned.
The response body shall contain a validity period during which the search result can be cached by the NF Service Consumer.

The response body shall contain an array of NF Profile objects and/or a map of NFInstanceInfo objects of NF instances if the NF service consumer indicated support of the Enh-NF-Discovery feature in the request.
If the NF Service Consumer is not allowed to discover the NF services for the requested NF type provided in the query parameters, the NRF shall return "403 Forbidden" response.

If the discovery request fails at the NRF due to errors in the input data in the URI query parameters, the NRF shall return "400 Bad Request" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.

If the verification of input attributes against the NF service consumer's certificate is unsuccessful, the request shall be rejected with "400 Bad Request" status code and the "cause" attribute set to "INVALID_CLIENT".
If the discovery request fails at the NRF due to NRF internal errors, the NRF shall return "500 Internal Server Error" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error.
In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code that contains a Location header with a URI pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance.
For those NF Instances of custom NF types, the "customInfo" attribute shall be returned by NRF, if available, as part of the NF Profiles returned in the discovery response.
The NRF shall include Vendor-Specific attributes in the returned NF Profile objects if those attributes were provided by the registered NF Instances.

If the response includes a map of NFInstanceInfo objects, the NF Service Consumer shall include the nrf-disc-uri parameter set to the API URI of the Nnrf_NFDiscovery service of the NRF holding the NF profile(s) when the request is addressed to a different NRF than the NRF holding the NF profile(s) and the nrfDiscApiUri attribute was received in the NFInstanceInfo object.
To discover an AUSF/UDM deployed in a partner PLMN, the NRF shall support the "subscription-based routing to a target core network" feature.
To discover an SMF deployed in a partner PLMN, the NRF shall support the "subscription-based routing to a target core network" feature.

If a BSF instance with a map of BsfInfo objects is discovered and the BsfInfo object matching the query parameters contains the "serviceScenarioInd" attribute, the NRF shall only include BsfInfo objects with the same "serviceScenarioInd" values as the matched BsfInfo object in the returned NF profile.
For service discovery in a different PLMN, the request shall include the identity of the PLMN of the home NRF in the "target-plmn-list" query parameter.
The NRF in the home PLMN shall not include IP addresses of NF (service) instances in NF profiles it includes in NF Discovery Response towards other PLMNs.
To discover an AUSF/UDM deployed in a partner PLMN, the NRF in the home PLMN shall support the "subscription-based routing to a target core network" feature.
To discover an SMF deployed in a partner PLMN, the NRF in the home PLMN shall support the "subscription-based routing to a target core network" feature.

If the NRF in Serving PLMN supports indirect communication with/without delegated discovery with NF selection at target domain and caches the response from NRF in Home PLMN for subsequent discovery result, it shall adjust the query parameter values when forwarding the discovery request to the NRF in Home PLMN to successfully process the discovery result.

The NRF in Serving PLMN shall lower the value of query parameters impacting the maximum number of candidates or maximum size of discovery result according to its own capability when forwarding the discovery request to the NRF in Home PLMN.
The NRF in Serving PLMN shall clear unsupported feature bits impacting the format of the discovery result when forwarding the discovery request to the NRF in Home PLMN.

Upon receiving a service discovery request, NRF-2 shall identify the next hop NRF based on the request information and locally stored information and redirect the service discovery request by returning HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect response.
The 307 Temporary Redirect response shall contain a Location header field whose host part represents NRF-3.
If NRF-2 does not have enough information to redirect the service discovery request, it shall respond with 404 Not Found.
Upon receiving 307 Temporary Redirect response, NRF-1 shall send the service discovery request to NRF-3 by using the URI contained in the Location header field of the 307 Temporary Redirect response.

Upon receiving a service discovery request, NRF-2 shall identify the next hop NRF based on the request information and locally stored information and forward the service discovery request to that NRF.
If NRF-2 does not have enough information to forward the service discovery request, it shall respond with 404 Not Found.
The NRF in the Local PLMN shall include the "gpsi" query parameter and set "target-nw-resolution" to true when the identity of the target PLMN is not known to the NF Service Consumer.
The NRF in the Local PLMN shall determine the identity of the Target PLMN and the URI of the Nnrf_NFDiscovery service of the NRF in the Target PLMN.
The NRF in the Serving PLMN shall return a status code to the NF Service Consumer in accordance with the result received from the NRF in the Home PLMN.

The NRF in the Home PLMN may provide either an array of NF Profile objects and/or a map of NFInstanceInfo objects, or indirect-communication indication IEs, depending on operator policy and the received indications.

If the NF Discovery Request includes the ind-com-with-del-disc IE set to true and indirect communication with delegated discovery with NF selection at target domain is preferred by the NRF in the Home PLMN, the response shall contain no NF profile objects and no NFInstanceInfo objects.

If the NF Discovery Request includes the ind-com-with-del-disc IE set to true and indirect communication with delegated discovery with NF selection at target domain is preferred by the NRF in the Home PLMN, the response shall set the indComWithDelDiscReq IE to true.

If the NF Discovery Request includes the ind-com-wo-del-disc IE set to true and indirect communication without delegated discovery with NF selection at target domain is preferred by the NRF in the Home PLMN, the response shall contain an array of NF Profile objects and/or a map of NFInstanceInfo objects that satisfy the search filter criteria.

If the NF Discovery Request includes the ind-com-wo-del-disc IE set to true and indirect communication without delegated discovery with NF selection at target domain is preferred by the NRF in the Home PLMN, the response shall set the indComWoDelDiscReq IE to true.

If either the indComWithDelDiscReq or the indComWoDelDiscReq IE is included in the search result, the indirect communication information shall only apply to the NF type requested in the Nnrf_NFDiscovery request unless the allNfTypesInd IE is set to true.

If the NRF in Serving PLMN supports the indirect communication with/without delegated discovery with NF selection at target domain features and caches the response from NRF in Home PLMN for subsequent discovery result, it shall adjust the query parameters when forwarding the discovery request to the NRF in Home PLMN.

The NRF in Serving PLMN shall lower the value of query parameters impacting the max number of candidates or max size of discovery result, such as limit, max-payload-size, and max-payload-size-ext, according to its own capability.

The NRF in Serving PLMN shall clear the feature bit impacting the format of the discovery result, such as Service-Map, Enh-NF-Discovery, Allowed-ruleset, DNN-List-Optimization, or Shared-Data, if not supported.
